s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the restructured PM SVANidhi scheme?
o: The first tranche was raised from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000.
Coverage was extended to census towns and peri-urban areas.
The second tranche was raised from ₹20,000 to ₹25,000.
The third tranche was raised above ₹50,000.
x: The third tranche remains ₹50,000, unchanged; only the first and second tranches were raised, to ₹15,000 and ₹25,000.

s: Which of the following correctly shows the loan tranches under PM SVANidhi?
x: PM SVANidhi provides successive loans of ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 to street vendors.

s: The restructured PM SVANidhi scheme expanded its coverage to include which areas?
o: Neither census towns nor peri-urban areas
x: The expanded PM SVANidhi coverage includes both census towns and peri-urban areas. Selecting either one alone misses the two-part expansion specified for the scheme.

s: The PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme has been extended up to which date?
x: PM SVANidhi, launched in 2020, has been extended from 31 December 2024 to 31 March 2030. The tempting option of 31 December 2024 is the earlier end date, not the extended one.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched about the restructured PM SVANidhi scheme?
o: Implementing institution – Department of Financial Services
Implementing institution – Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card – After repayment of the first tranche
x: The UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card comes after repaying the second tranche, not the first, so that pair is wrong. Cashback is up to ₹1,600, and MoHUA with the Department of Financial Services are the nodal bodies (SIDBI implements the scheme).

s: What interest subsidy does PM SVANidhi, the scheme for street vendors, provide?
x: PM SVANidhi provides a 7% interest subsidy and is implemented by SIDBI.

s: Which institution implements the restructured PM SVANidhi scheme?
x: PM SVANidhi (nodal MoHUA and DFS) is implemented by SIDBI.

s: What is the outlay of the PM SVANidhi scheme extended till 31 March 2030?
x: The extended scheme has an outlay of ₹7,332 crore, targeting 1.15 crore beneficiaries.

s: Under PM SVANidhi, after repaying which loan does a street vendor get a UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card?
x: The RuPay Credit Card is given after the second tranche is repaid.

s: How many beneficiaries does the restructured PM SVANidhi aim to cover?
x: The target is 1.15 crore beneficiaries, including 50 lakh new ones.

s: Where is the headquarters of SIDBI, which implements the PM SVANidhi scheme?
x: SIDBI, set up on 2 April 1990, has its head office in Lucknow.

s: In which year was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?
x: SIDBI was set up on 2 April 1990 under the SIDBI Act, 1989.

s: The amended Schedule I of MGNREGA links minimum water-works spending to which assessment?
o: CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment
x: The amendment is based on the CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment, not the Census of India.

s: By which year did the Jal Jeevan Mission (2019) originally aim to provide tap water to every rural household?
x: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 with the original target of tap water to every rural household by 2024.

s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, which Andhra Pradesh district reported the lowest tap-water coverage (35.55%)?
x: Palnadu had the lowest coverage at 35.55%, while YSR district reported 100%.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh district reported 100% tap-water coverage under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
x: YSR district has 100% coverage; Palnadu is lowest at 35.55%.

s: Under amended Schedule I of MGNREGA, semi-critical blocks must spend at least what share on water works?
x: Semi-critical blocks: 40%; over-exploited/critical: 65%; safe: 30%.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rural tap-water coverage under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
x: About 70.5 lakh rural households (73.82%) in AP have tap connections, up from 32.18% in 2019.

s: During 2014–2021, India's under-five mortality rate declined from 45 to how many per 1,000?
x: The under-five mortality rate fell from 45 to 31 per 1,000 during 2014–2021.

s: India's Universal Immunisation Programme covers how many infants every year?
x: UIP covers 2.6 crore infants and 2.9 crore pregnant women each year, making it the world's largest.

s: Which digital platforms are linked with India's immunisation efforts (June 2025)?
x: Co-WIN and U-WIN are the immunisation platforms; DigiLocker relates to CBSE marksheets and NOTTO to transplant data.

s: Which of the following pairs of immunisation milestones is correctly matched?
x: The MR campaign ran from 2017–2019. Tetanus elimination was in 2015, yaws-free status in 2016 and the Champion Award on 6 March 2024.

s: In which year was the Zero Dose Implementation Plan for immunisation launched?
x: The Zero Dose Implementation Plan dates to 2024; Mission Indradhanush was 2014 and UIP 1985.

s: Which country did WHO validate as the first to eliminate mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B?
x: WHO validated Maldives as the first country to achieve this triple elimination.

s: What is the official name of the programme linked to Himachal Pradesh’s literacy achievement and the ULLAS Mela?
x: ULLAS stands for the New India Literacy Programme. The other options are immunisation-related programmes and are not the literacy programme associated with ULLAS.

s: Which digital platform under India’s immunisation ecosystem caters to pregnant women and children up to 16 years?
x: U-WIN caters to pregnant women and children up to 16 years. CO-WIN, eVIN and NCCMIS are other digital systems listed in the immunisation ecosystem, making them plausible but incorrect alternatives.

s: When did India's COVID-19 vaccination drive begin?
x: COVID vaccination began on 16 January 2021 and crossed 220 crore doses by January 2023.

s: According to the Lancet study, which country had the highest number of zero-dose children in 2023?
x: Nigeria had the highest number; India was second. The global total was 15.7 million.

s: What is the IA2030 goal concerning zero-dose children?
x: IA2030 aims to halve the number of zero-dose children by 2030. The alternatives change either the target, the direction of change, or the year.

s: In which year was India's last polio case reported?
x: The last case was on 13 January 2011 in West Bengal; WHO certified the region on 27 March 2014.

s: Under the IA2030 framework, a 'zero-dose' child is one who has not received any dose of which vaccine by age one?
x: A zero-dose child has received no dose of DTP vaccine by age one.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's Universal Immunisation Programme covers 12 diseases.
2. India had the highest number of zero-dose children in the world in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: UIP covers 12 diseases (11 nationwide, 1 endemic). India had the second-highest number of zero-dose children (1.44 million), after Nigeria.

s: The Zero Dose Implementation Plan (2024) covers how many districts?
x: The plan covers 143 districts in 11 States.

s: In which year was the Universal Immunisation Programme launched in India?
x: UIP began in 1985; 1974 is the year of WHO's Expanded Programme on Immunization.

s: In which year was Mission Indradhanush launched?
x: Mission Indradhanush began in 2014; Intensified Mission Indradhanush followed in 2017.

s: In which year did WHO start the Expanded Programme on Immunization?
x: WHO's EPI began in 1974; India's UIP followed in 1985.

s: In which year was India declared Yaws-free?
x: India became Yaws-free in 2016; maternal and neonatal tetanus was eliminated in 2015.

s: On which date did WHO certify the South-East Asia region, including India, polio-free?
x: India's last case was 13 January 2011; WHO certified the region on 27 March 2014.

s: What monthly wage did Maharashtra promise to pay Anshakalin Stri Parichars by December 2025?
x: Maharashtra promised to raise the monthly wage of Anshakalin Stri Parichars to ₹6,000 by December 2025. Their wage had remained stagnant at ₹3,000 per month since 2016, making ₹3,000 the key trap.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's pharmaceutical sector?
o: It is projected to grow from $50 billion to $130 billion by 2030
It provides 40% of the world's vaccines
Branded generics make up 87% of the Indian market
x: India provides 50–60% of the world's vaccines, not 40%. The other statements are correct.

s: What did the Nagpur labour court state in 2023 regarding Anshakalin Stri Parichars in Maharashtra?
o: They were introduced under the National Rural Health Mission.
They must immediately receive parity with MPWs.
They are classified as volunteers paid only by incentives.
They deserve protection under the Minimum Wages Act, with implementation left to the State.
x: The Nagpur labour court held that Anshakalin Stri Parichars deserve protection under the Minimum Wages Act, while leaving implementation to the State. It did not mandate parity with MPWs, which is the key trap in the second option.

s: What decision was taken by the Andhra Pradesh Health Department regarding Jan Aushadhi stores?
o: To set up Jan Aushadhi stores only in 16 Government General Hospitals
To set up Jan Aushadhi stores in all Government General Hospitals
To set up a Jan Aushadhi store only at Nandyal Government General Hospital
To first set up Jan Aushadhi stores in all District and Area Hospitals
x: The decision was to set up Jan Aushadhi stores in all Government General Hospitals in Andhra Pradesh. The proposal for District and Area Hospitals was only at the feasibility-study stage, while the review covered 16 GGHs and noted that Nandyal GGH had no private medical store.

s: Under what condition may branded drugs be stocked in Jan Aushadhi stores?
o: Only with prior approval, when no generic alternative exists
Without prior approval, even when a generic exists
With prior approval, even when a generic exists
Without prior approval, when no generic exists
x: Branded drugs need prior approval and are allowed only when no generic alternative exists.

s: Under PM-BJAP, at what level is the profit margin on medicines at Jan Aushadhi stores capped?
x: PM-BJAP caps the profit margin at 15%; its software is developed by the Department of Pharmaceuticals.

s: The cough syrup deaths mentioned in the drug-safety context occurred in which countries?
x: The countries identified were Gambia and Uzbekistan. Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom and China appear in other contexts but were not the countries linked to these cough syrup deaths.

s: In which year were ASHAs introduced under the National Rural Health Mission?
x: ASHA was introduced under NRHM in 2005; ASHAs are classified as volunteers paid by incentives.

s: Which committee defined universal health care as care for all irrespective of ability to pay?
x: The Bhore Committee (1946) defined universal health care as care for all, irrespective of ability to pay.

s: In which year was the National Health Policy that set a public health spending target of 2.5% of GDP issued?
x: The National Health Policy dates to 2017; its public health spending target is 2.5% of GDP.

s: According to WHO, how many drugs in developing countries are fake or substandard?
x: The WHO estimate is 1 in 10 drugs, not 1 in 20.

s: The emergency preparedness directive issued amid India–Pakistan tensions included 'CBRN' preparedness. What is the full form of CBRN?
x: CBRN = Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear; CBRN preparedness was among the directive's measures.

s: PMJAY provides health cover of how much per household per year?
x: PMJAY (2018) gives ₹5 lakh per household per year for in-patient care.

s: Which body provides the software for PM-BJAP Jan Aushadhi stores?
x: PM-BJAP's software comes from the Department of Pharmaceuticals; the profit margin is capped at 15%.

s:
Consider the following statements about Anshakalin Stri Parichars (ASPs) of Maharashtra:
1. They predate ASHAs.
2. Their wage had been ₹3,000 a month since 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: ASPs are older than ASHAs, and their wage was stuck at ₹3,000 a month since 2016.

s: Which of the following statements about CDSCO is correct?
o: It is an independent statutory regulator
It reports to DGHS under the Health Ministry
It works under the Department of Pharmaceuticals
It licenses all drugs, leaving no role to States
x: CDSCO is not independent: it reports to DGHS and the Health Ministry, and States also license.

s: What was India's public health spending as a share of GDP in 2022 (World Bank)?
x: Public health spending was 1.3% of GDP against a world average of 6.1%.

s: According to the Health of the Nation 2025 report, what share of Indians could identify heart symptoms in 2024?
x: Only 25% of Indians could identify heart symptoms in 2024, not 50%.

s: In the NFSA ration-card verification, which category was identified using MCA data?
x: MCA data identified company directors; the Income Tax Department identified taxpayers and MoRTH four-wheeler owners.

s: As per WHO's 2023 guidance, within what time should stroke rehabilitation ideally begin?
x: WHO's 2023 guidance says stroke rehabilitation should begin within 24–48 hours.

s: Which set of measures was associated with addressing the nutrition concerns highlighted in the ICMR-INDIAB 2025 discussion?
o: Revised Schedule M, Drugs and Cosmetics Act, and Article 21
National Rural Health Mission, Minimum Wages Act protection, and MTP Act
International Year of Millets 2023, CBSE sugar boards, and FSSAI Front-of-Pack Labelling proposals
White rice, milled grains, and added sugars
x: The relevant measures were the International Year of Millets 2023, CBSE sugar boards in schools, and FSSAI Front-of-Pack Labelling proposals. The other options combine unrelated legal, health-worker or dietary references.

s: According to the ICMR 2023 finding cited in the ICMR-INDIAB 2025 discussion, diabetes affected which population?
x: The ICMR 2023 finding reported diabetes in over 100 million adults. The figures of more than 12 million and 0.4 million relate to child obesity, while 1,21,077 was the number of adults surveyed in ICMR-INDIAB.

s: What did the ‘Thali’ framework identify as a major gap between the poorest and richest households?
o: Cereal consumption, while PDS subsidy favours vegetables
Fruit consumption, while PDS subsidy favours milk
Milk consumption, while PDS subsidy favours pulses
Pulses consumption, while PDS subsidy favours cereals
x: The framework identified a pulses consumption gap between the poorest and richest households, while the PDS subsidy favours cereals. The other options change both the food category and the subsidy pattern.

s: As per the ICMR-INDIAB 2025 survey, carbohydrates contributed what share of daily calories?
x: Carbohydrates supplied 62% of daily calories among 1,21,077 adults surveyed across 36 States and UTs.

s: In the stroke-awareness campaign 'FAST', what does the letter 'A' stand for?
x: FAST stands for Face, Arms, Speech and Time.

s: What did the ‘Thali’ framework find regarding the affordability of two thali meals a day?
o: About 63% of rural and 25–26% of urban households could not afford them
About 20% of rural and 50% of urban households could not afford them
About 50% of rural and 20% of urban households could not afford them
About 10% of rural and 15% of urban households could not afford them
x: The finding was that about 50% of rural households and 20% of urban households could not afford two thali meals a day. Reversing the rural and urban figures produces the most direct trap in this question.

s: Which department flagged approximately 1.17 crore ration-card holders as potentially ineligible under the NFSA, 2013, through inter-ministerial data matching?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Department of Food and Public Distribution
x: The Department of Food and Public Distribution flagged approximately 1.17 crore potentially ineligible ration-card holders through inter-ministerial data matching. The Income Tax Department was one of the databases used for verification, not the department that issued the list.

s: Who is responsible for deleting ineligible ration cards flagged in the NFSA verification exercise?
x: Deletion is the responsibility of States and UTs; the Centre only provides the data.

s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the rural population?
x: The Act covers 67% of the population: 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population.

s: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, what were the prescribed prices through the Targeted Public Distribution System for rice, wheat and coarse grains, respectively?
x: The prescribed prices were ₹3 per kg for rice, ₹2 per kg for wheat and ₹1 per kg for coarse grains through the Targeted Public Distribution System. The other options interchange these prices among the three grain categories.

s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers what share of the urban population?
x: NFSA covers 75% rural and 50% urban population, 67% overall.

s: Which tool does the Department of Food and Public Distribution use to flag ineligible ration-card holders?
x: The API-based Rightful Targeting Dashboard matches ration data with other databases to flag ineligible holders.

s: In the NFSA ration-card verification, which category had the most flagged holders?
x: Income Tax data flagged 94.71 lakh taxpayers, the largest group.

s: Under which scheme were NFSA foodgrains made free?
x: Foodgrains under NFSA were made free under PMGKAY.

s: Which State was declared fully literate with a literacy rate of 99.30% on International Literacy Day 2025?
x: Himachal Pradesh was declared fully literate after attaining 99.30% literacy, above the 95% benchmark. Mizoram, Tripura and Goa were already identified as fully literate States before this declaration.

s: Which State was declared India's first fully digitally literate State on 21 August 2025?
x: Kerala was declared India's first fully digitally literate State under the Digi Kerala programme, modelled on Digi Pullampara.

s: ULLAS treats full literacy as at least what share of literacy among people aged 15 years and above?
x: ULLAS uses a 95% benchmark for those aged 15 and above, including digital and financial literacy.

s: Which combination of organisations and community groups served as volunteers in the Digi Pullampara model?
o: KILA, Economics & Statistics Department, NSS and TRIFED
NSS, Kudumbashree, SC/ST promoters and library council
Kudumbashree, KFON, K-SMART and library council
SC/ST promoters, IIT Delhi, NSS and KILA
x: The volunteer network comprised NSS, Kudumbashree, SC/ST promoters and the library council. KILA and the Economics & Statistics Department had other roles, while KFON, K-SMART and IIT Delhi were not listed as Pullampara volunteers.

s:
Assertion (A): Digi Kerala 2.0 included service access as one of its objectives.
Reason (R): K-SMART was intended to digitise all services of local self-government bodies.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the K-SMART objective explains the service-access component of Digi Kerala 2.0. Digi Kerala 2.0 was announced by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, while K-SMART concerned digitisation of all local self-government services.

s: Which was the first fully literate State under ULLAS?
x: Mizoram was first (2024), followed by Tripura and Goa; Himachal Pradesh is the 4th.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about literacy firsts in India?
o: Mizoram was the first fully literate State under ULLAS
Ladakh was the first fully literate Union Territory
Himachal Pradesh was the first fully literate State
Kerala was the first fully digitally literate State
x: Himachal Pradesh (99.30%) is the 4th fully literate State, after Mizoram, Tripura and Goa.

s: Which is India's first cooperative ride-hailing platform?
x: Bharat Taxi is the first cooperative ride-hailing platform.

s: Master trainers for Digi Kerala were trained at KILA. What is the full form of KILA?
o: Kerala Institute of Learning and Awareness
x: KILA is the Kerala Institute of Local Administration.

s: Which panchayat became the first fully digitally literate panchayat in Kerala in September 2022?
x: Pullampara panchayat in Thiruvananthapuram became Kerala's first fully digitally literate panchayat; Digi Kerala was modelled on it.

s: What was launched in beta on 1 September 2025 as India's first AI-powered translation platform for tribal languages?
x: Adi Vaani was launched in beta by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs as India's first AI-powered translation platform for tribal languages. PM JANMAN, Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan and Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh are associated contexts or initiatives, not the translation platform.

s: Which of the following Adi Vaani beta language–State pairs is correctly matched?
x: The beta pairs are Santali–Odisha, Bhili–Madhya Pradesh, Mundari–Jharkhand and Gondi–Chhattisgarh.

s: On the Adi Sanskriti platform, with which body is Adi Haat linked?
x: Adi Haat is linked with TRIFED, not the Ministry of Textiles.

s: Which institution led the consortium that developed the beta version of Adi Vaani?
x: An IIT Delhi-led consortium built Adi Vaani at about one-tenth the cost of commercial AI; BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad and IIIT Nava Raipur were participants.

s: Besides PM JANMAN, with which initiative was the tribal-language platform Adi Vaani linked?
x: Adi Vaani was linked with PM JANMAN and the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, not Digi Kerala.

s: The Gutti Koya tribals were displaced by anti-Maoist operations from which State?
x: They were displaced from Chhattisgarh, where they are recognised as Scheduled Tribes, unlike in AP and Telangana.

s: Under Section 3.1(m) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006, what are Gutti Koya tribals displaced before the cut-off date entitled to?
x: Section 3.1(m) entitles tribals displaced before 13 December 2005 to alternative forest land.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the displacement of Gutti Koya tribals?
o: Strategic hamleting was borrowed from the US war strategy in Vietnam
The strategy had earlier been used in Mizoram during the 1960s
Strategic hamleting moved about 50,000 Gonds away from roads into forest interiors
The NCST suggested alignment with the UN Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement
x: Strategic hamleting moved about 50,000 Gonds into roadside camps, not into forest interiors.

s: Adi Vaani was launched under Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh by which Ministry?
x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs launched the Adi Vaani beta on 1 September 2025.

s: What is Adi Vishwavidyalaya on the Adi Sanskriti platform?
o: Digital tribal art academy with 45 online courses
x: Adi Vishwavidyalaya is a digital tribal art academy with 45 online courses; Adi Haat is the marketplace.

s: What is the Forest Rights Act cut-off date for displaced tribals to claim alternative forest land?
x: Under Section 3.1(m) of FRA 2006, tribals displaced before 13 December 2005 get alternative forest land.

s: In which State are the Gutti Koya, displaced into Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, recognised as a Scheduled Tribe?
x: Gutti Koya are ST in Chhattisgarh but not in AP or Telangana, where they now live.

s: Which platform of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is envisioned as the world's first digital university for tribal art forms?
x: Adi Sanskriti is planned as the world's first digital university for tribal art forms; Adi Vaani is the AI translator.

s: Under the Bru Rehabilitation Plan, 2019, in which State were the Bru people settled?
x: The Bru were settled in Tripura under the 2019 plan.

s: The Unique Disability ID (UDID) system covers how many disabilities?
x: UDID covers 21 disabilities; less than 40% of persons with disabilities have a UDID card.

s: The Washington Group–Short Set for disability data can be aligned with how many categories of the RPwD Act, 2016?
x: It can be aligned with the 21 disability categories of the RPwD Act, 2016.

s: Which of the following statements about the Unique Disability ID (UDID) system is incorrect?
o: Tamil Nadu, Meghalaya, Odisha and Karnataka have above 50% coverage.
West Bengal has only 6% UDID coverage.
Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh and Mizoram have 80%+ applications pending for over 6 months.
x: The incorrect statement is that the ADIP scheme covers 21 disabilities; the 21-disability coverage is a feature of UDID, while ADIP provides aids such as wheelchairs, prostheses, hearing aids and Braille slates. The other statements correctly identify the States and coverage or delay figures.

s: Census 2011 collected disability data through medical yes/no questions in how many categories?
x: Census 2011 asked medical yes/no questions in only 8 categories. The RPwD Act, 2016 recognises 21 categories, so experts suggest the Washington Group Short Set.

s: Which of the following disability-related measure–year pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Policy for Persons with Disabilities – 2006
x: The National Policy dates to 2006; the RCI Act is from 1992, the National Trust Act from 1999 and UNCRPD ratification from 2007.

s: In which year was the Accessible India Campaign, also known as Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, launched?
x: The Accessible India Campaign was associated with 2015. The other years belong to the National Trust Act, Mental Health Care Act and Harmonized Accessibility Guidelines respectively.

s: In which year were the Harmonized Accessibility Guidelines issued?
x: The Harmonized Accessibility Guidelines were issued in 2021; the Mental Health Care Act dates from 2017.

s: What was the disability prevalence in India recorded by Census 2011?
x: Census 2011 recorded 26.8 million persons with disabilities, or 2.21%.

s: Which statement correctly describes the funding pattern of the UDID sub-scheme?
x: Funding for the UDID sub-scheme was reduced during 2019–2023. The alternatives incorrectly describe the direction of change or the introduction of the sub-scheme.

s: Why is Census 2027 significant for India?
x: Census 2027 will be India's first digital Census, the first since 2011.

s: Which of the following disability-related pairs is correctly matched?
o: ADIP – aids and appliances such as wheelchairs and hearing aids
x: ADIP gives aids and appliances. UDID covers 21 disabilities, Census 2011 recorded 2.21% (4.52% is NFHS-5) and the RCI Act is of 1992.

s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 raised the recognised disability categories from 7 to how many?
x: The RPwD Act, 2016 recognises 21 categories, up from 7 in the 1995 Act.

s: Which department runs the Unique Disability ID (UDID) system?
x: UDID is run by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).

s: In which year did India ratify the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities?
x: India ratified the UNCRPD in 2007.

s: Under the proposed EPFO withdrawal norms, what minimum balance must be kept in the EPF account?
x: The proposed minimum balance is 25%; education withdrawals are allowed up to 10 times and marriage withdrawals up to 5 times.

s: From which grade does the National Education Policy, 2020 provide vocational exposure?
x: NEP 2020 provides vocational exposure from Grade 6.

s: Who released the Draft National Labour and Employment Policy — Shram Shakti Niti 2025 for public consultation?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
x: The Union Labour Ministry released the draft Shram Shakti Niti 2025 for public consultation.

s: By which year does Shram Shakti Niti 2025 target a female labour force participation rate of 35%?
x: The female LFPR target is 35% by 2030, not 2035.

s: In the context of Building a Shikshit Bharat, in which area has the Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) highlighted weakness?
x: ASER has highlighted weak foundational literacy and numeracy; the 1.5% of GDP figure relates to recommended R&D spending, not ASER.

s: Under which phase of the Draft Shram Shakti Niti 2025 is paperless governance proposed?
x: Paperless governance is proposed under Phase III, beyond 2030.

s: Which monitoring mechanisms are proposed under the Draft Shram Shakti Niti 2025?
o: One Nation Integrated Workforce and Annual National Labour Report to Parliament
Labour & Employment Policy Evaluation Index and District Employment Facilitation Cells
Green Jobs Index and Annual National Labour Report to Parliament
Labour & Employment Policy Evaluation Index and Annual National Labour Report to Parliament
x: The draft proposes the Labour & Employment Policy Evaluation Index (LPEI) and an Annual National Labour Report to Parliament for monitoring.

s: What is the approximate corpus of the EPFO?
x: The EPFO corpus is more than ₹26 lakh crore (with 30 crore+ accounts, about 7 crore of them active).

s: Which of the following was NOT among the listed initiatives for harnessing India's demographic dividend?
x: The listed initiative was Stand-up India, not Digital India; PM-DAKSH and Atal Tinkering Labs were also on the list.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EPFO premature withdrawals and proposed reforms?
o: 95% of final settlements in 2024–25 were premature
Withdrawal categories are proposed to be cut from 13 to 3
EPS pension eligibility requires 5 years of pensionable service
The waiting period for premature final settlement was raised from 2 to 12 months
x: EPS pension eligibility requires 10 years of pensionable service, not 5.

s: Under Para 69(2) of the EPF Scheme, 1952, a member can make a full withdrawal after how long of unemployment?
x: Para 69(2) permits full withdrawal after two months of unemployment; twelve months is the proposed waiting period for premature final settlement.

s: What share of PMJAY spending goes to private hospitals?
x: Private hospitals receive two-thirds of PMJAY spending, not one-third.

s: India, the largest groundwater user, accounts for about what share of global groundwater extraction?
x: India is the largest groundwater user, with about 25% of global extraction.

s: What share of India's graduates are job-ready?
x: Only 42–43% of graduates are job-ready.

s: What was the enrolment in India's ITIs in 2022, a 48% seat utilisation?
x: 2022 enrolment was 12 lakh against 25 lakh seats in over 14,000 ITIs.

s: The lifelong upskilling programme 'SkillsFuture' belongs to which country?
x: SkillsFuture is Singapore's lifelong upskilling programme; Singapore also offers VET-to-university pathways.

s: The missed Skill India target was to skill how many people by 2022?
x: The Skill India target of skilling 400 million people by 2022 was missed.

s: Germany's dual system combines upper-secondary vocational education with which of the following?
x: Germany's dual system combines upper-secondary VET with paid apprenticeships; lifelong upskilling and university pathways describe Singapore.

s: With which company did MSDE sign the 'AI Careers for Women' MoU in April 2025?
x: MSDE signed it with Microsoft (implemented by Edunet Foundation) for 30 Centres of Excellence in women's colleges.

s: Which body signed the MSME Credit Facilitation Programme MoUs with private banks on 11 August 2025?
x: NSIC, under the Ministry of MSME, signed MoUs with Axis, Dhanlaxmi, Karnataka, AU Small Finance and IndusInd banks.

s: Which of the following MoU – purpose pairs is correctly matched?
o: NSIC–Axis Bank – AI careers for women
DGT–Autodesk – design and make skills in ITIs and NSTIs
x: The DGT–Autodesk MoU (6 November 2025) covers design and make skills in 14,682 ITIs and 33 NSTIs.

s: Under the new EPFO norms, withdrawal categories have been reduced from 13 to how many?
x: Withdrawal categories were cut from 13 to 3: essential needs, housing and special circumstances.

s: Pension eligibility under the Employees' Pension Scheme requires how many years of pensionable service?
x: EPS pension needs 10 years of pensionable service.

s: What is the EPFO wage ceiling per month?
x: The EPFO wage ceiling is ₹15,000 a month.

s: How many Centres of Excellence in women's colleges are planned under the MSDE-Microsoft 'AI Careers for Women' MoU?
x: It sets up 30 CoEs in women's colleges across 6 States.

s: Under CBSE's two Class 10 exams from 2026–27, students failing in how many subjects can use the second exam?
x: Only compartment students failing in 1–2 subjects can use the second examination; those failing 3 cannot.

s: The Right to Education Act, 2009, which provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years, implements which constitutional provision?
x: The RTE Act implements Article 21-A and covers free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 years. The other Articles listed do not represent the constitutional provision identified with this RTE mandate.

s: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act reserves what share of Class 1 seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged and EWS children?
x: The RTE quota is 25%, not 15%.

s: CBSE's optional May Class 10 exam (from 2026–27) allows improvement in up to three subjects from among which subjects?
o: Science, Mathematics and Social Science only
Science, Mathematics, Social Science and two languages
Two languages and Social Science only
Science, Mathematics and two languages only
x: Improvement in up to three subjects is allowed from among Science, Mathematics, Social Science and two languages.

s: Under the CBSE two-examination system, which score is counted?
x: The better of the two scores counts; Essential Repeat students cannot take the second examination.

s: By which month are the results of CBSE's mandatory first Class 10 board examination (mid-February) to be declared?
x: First-exam results come by April; the optional May exam's results come by June.

s: Which of the following statements about the Right to Education Act, 2009, is incorrect?
o: It provides for no detention till Class 8.
It permits detention of children from Class 5 onwards.
It provides for School Management Committees.
x: The incorrect statement is that detention is permitted from Class 5 onwards; the stated provision is no detention till Class 8. The Act also prohibits capitation fees and provides for School Management Committees.

s: For AP private schools under the RTE quota, by which date must children following the State syllabus complete 5 years?
x: Age 5 must be completed by 1 June for the State syllabus, and by 31 March for IB/CBSE/ICSE.

s: Who heads the 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026?
x: Sanjay Jaiswal chairs the 31-member JPC (21 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the JPC on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026?
o: 21 members are from the Lok Sabha.
The nodal ministry for the FCRA is the Ministry of Finance.
10 members are from the Rajya Sabha.
x: The nodal ministry for the FCRA is the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance.

s: Which description correctly characterises a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
o: It is an executive committee that continues until dissolved by the President.
It is a permanent committee comprising members of only the Lok Sabha.
It is an ad hoc committee comprising members of both Houses and ends after completing its task.
It is a judicial committee comprising members of only the Rajya Sabha.
x: A Joint Parliamentary Committee is ad hoc, includes members of both Houses, and ends after completing its task. The other descriptions wrongly make it permanent, executive, judicial or limited to one House.

s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
x: The 31-member JPC on the VBSA Bill is chaired by D. Purandeswari; Sanjay Jaiswal chairs the FCRA JPC.

s: How many members does the JPC on the One Nation One Election (129th Amendment) Bill have?
x: The ONOE JPC under P.P. Chaudhary has 39 members: 27 Lok Sabha and 12 Rajya Sabha.

s: Which MP chaired the JPCs on both the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026 and the Biological Diversity Amendment Bill, 2021?
x: Sanjay Jaiswal chaired both JPCs; P.P. Chaudhary chaired the ONOE and Personal Data Protection JPCs.

s: Which of the following pairs (Bill – JPC chair) is correctly matched?
o: Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 – Jagdambika Pal
Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019 – Bhupender Yadav
Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Bill, 2022 – Rajendra Agrawal
x: Aparajita Sarangi chairs the 130th Amendment JPC; the Corporate Laws, PDP and Multi-State Cooperative JPCs were chaired by Sudheer Gupta, P.P. Chaudhary and C.P. Joshi.

s: Which Article of the Constitution lets each House of Parliament make its own rules of procedure?
x: Article 118 empowers each House to make its own rules of procedure.

s: Who chaired the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
x: The JPC on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was chaired by Jagdambika Pal.

s: Who chairs the JPC on the One Nation One Election (129th Constitution Amendment) Bill, 2024?
x: The 39-member JPC on the ONOE Bills is chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.

s: Who chaired the JPC on the Forest Conservation Amendment Bill, 2023?
x: Rajendra Agrawal chaired the JPC on the Forest Conservation Amendment Bill, 2023.

s: Who chaired the JPC on the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019?
x: P.P. Chaudhary chaired the PDP Bill 2019 JPC, and also the ONOE JPC.

s: What is the tenure of a Departmentally-Related Standing Committee (DRSC)?
x: DRSCs are standing committees with tenure up to one year; a JPC is ad hoc and ends after its task.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the DRSCs reconstituted for 2026-27?
o: Ministers can be members of these committees.
They examine Demands for Grants, bills and annual reports.
Eight of them work under the Rajya Sabha Chairman.
x: Ministers cannot be members of DRSCs.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on Finance for 2026-27?
x: Bhartruhari Mahtab heads Finance; Shashi Tharoor heads External Affairs and Radha Mohan Singh heads Defence.

s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:
1. A Joint Parliamentary Committee is ad hoc and ends after its task.
2. A Departmentally-Related Standing Committee is a standing committee with tenure up to one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: a JPC is ad hoc, while a DRSC is a standing committee with tenure up to one year.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on External Affairs for 2026-27?
x: Shashi Tharoor chairs the External Affairs DRSC.

s: Which institution was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 October 2026 as a Special Purpose Vehicle for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring in the transport and logistics sector?
o: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan
x: The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) was approved as an SPV for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring. The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and National Logistics Policy are separate initiatives, while IWAI is associated with inland waterways.

s: Central projects of what cost are technically appraised by the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA)?
x: ITLA undertakes technical appraisal of central projects of ₹500 crore or more; it also prepares a 10+ year National Transport Master Plan.

s: Which top telecom decision-making body was abolished by the Centre after functioning for 37 years?
x: The Centre abolished the Digital Communications Commission, or DCC, which had served as the top telecom decision body for 37 years. Telecom Commission was its former name, while the Narco-Coordination Centre is a drug-control mechanism.

s: Who released the strategic action plan Mission Rangeen Machhli–2031 at Agatti, Lakshadweep?
x: The Vice-President released Mission Rangeen Machhli–2031 for ornamental fisheries at Agatti, Lakshadweep.

s: For whom is training meant under Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031?
o: Coastal fishers, youth and women SHGs
x: The Mission's training covers coastal fishers, youth and women self-help groups, not coastal fishers alone.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the RoDTEP scheme is incorrect?
o: It was notified by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.
RoDTEP replaced MEIS and is WTO-compliant.
The scheme became effective from 1 January 2021.
x: The incorrect statement is that RoDTEP was notified by the Department of Revenue through CBIC. It was notified by the Department of Commerce through DGFT; implementation is carried out by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.

s: RoDTEP, in force from 1 January 2021, replaced which export scheme?
x: RoDTEP replaced MEIS, which faced WTO objections; RoDTEP is WTO-compliant.

s: In which year was the Telecom Commission, later renamed the Digital Communications Commission, set up?
x: The Telecom Commission was set up in 1989 and renamed DCC in 2018; it was abolished after 37 years.

s: After the DCC was abolished, which body now examines telecom projects of ₹500-1,000 crore?
x: Projects of ₹500–1,000 crore go to the Expenditure Finance Committee; the Telecom Secretary approves up to ₹100 crore and the Minister up to ₹500 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RoDTEP scheme:
1. It is notified by the Department of Commerce through DGFT.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: DGFT notifies RoDTEP and CBIC implements it, not the other way round.

s: Which plan, with a horizon of more than 10 years, will the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) prepare?
x: ITLA will prepare the National Transport Master Plan covering roads, rail, ports, aviation, waterways and logistics.

s: For which sector is Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031 a strategic action plan?
x: Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031 of the Department of Fisheries is for ornamental (colourful) fish.

s: Which department leads Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031, linked with PMMSY?
x: The Department of Fisheries leads it; it is linked with PMMSY.

s: The 23rd Law Commission of India is which kind of body?
x: The Law Commission is an executive body, neither constitutional nor statutory, advising the Ministry of Law and Justice.

s: Who is the full-time chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission?
x: Justice Dinesh Maheshwari has been full-time chair since 15 April 2025; the term runs to 31 August 2027.

s: Which of the following is included in the current mandate of the 23rd Law Commission?
x: The 23rd Law Commission's mandate includes examining a Uniform Civil Code; its recommendations are not binding.

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission keep the States' share of the divisible pool?
x: The 16th FC kept vertical devolution at 41%, the same as the 15th FC, and declined demands for 50%.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission award:
1. It keeps the States' share of the divisible pool at 41%.
2. It raises the weight of income distance to 45%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: income distance was cut to 42.5% from 45%.

s: Which criterion was newly introduced by the 16th Finance Commission for sharing taxes among States?
x: Contribution to GDP is the new criterion; the other three were already used and only had their weights changed.

s: Who chairs the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC, a constitutional body under Article 280, with an award period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s: Who has been the Chairperson of the Press Council of India since 24 April 2026?
x: Former SC judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai has chaired the PCI since 24 April 2026 for three years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Press Council of India?
o: It is a statutory, autonomous and quasi-judicial body.
It is headquartered in New Delhi.
It has a Chairperson and 28 members.
It is a constitutional body created under Article 19(1)(a).
x: The PCI is statutory, under the Press Council Act, 1978; Article 19(1)(a) only guarantees press freedom.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council of India:
1. It has 13 journalist members among its 28 members.
2. It has 5 Members of Parliament: 3 from Lok Sabha and 2 from Rajya Sabha.
3. National Press Day is observed on 16 November.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the PCI has 13 journalists, 6 owners, 5 MPs, 3 institutional nominees and 1 news agency member; National Press Day is 16 November.

s: The Telangana Senior Citizens Commission has one Chief Commissioner and how many Commissioners?
x: The Commission has 1 Chief Commissioner (Justice E. Tirumala Devi) and 2 Commissioners.

s: Who chooses the Chairperson of the Press Council of India?
o: President on the advice of the Prime Minister
Chief Justice of India and Law Minister
Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker and one PCI member
x: The PCI Chairperson is chosen by a panel of the RS Chairman, LS Speaker and one member of the Council.

s: Which report of the Law Commission of India recommended retaining the sedition provision (Section 124A of the IPC)?
x: The 22nd Law Commission's 279th Report, 'Usage of the Law of Sedition' (2023), recommended retaining Section 124A.

s: What did the Law Commission's 279th Report (2023) recommend on sedition?
o: Retain Section 124A with safeguards and higher punishment
Make sedition a bailable civil wrong
x: It said to keep Section 124A, add the Kedar Nath Singh (1962) safeguards and raise the punishment.

s: What weight did the 16th Finance Commission give to income distance in its formula for sharing taxes among States?
x: The 16th FC cut the weight of income distance from 45% to 42.5%; population (2011) got 17.5% and demographic performance 10%.

s: Which of the following can the Press Council of India NOT do?
x: PCI can warn, admonish and censure but cannot impose criminal penalties.

s: What is the award period of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC (Arvind Panagariya) covers 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s: When was NITI Aayog set up?
x: NITI Aayog, an executive body, was set up on 1 January 2015.

s: Suresh N. Patel, Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, earlier held which post?
o: MD and CEO of Indian Bank
x: Suresh N. Patel is a former CVC, not an RBI official.

s: Which serving RBI Deputy Governor is a member of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat?
x: Shirish Chandra Murmu (RBI Deputy Governor) is a member; N.S. Vishwanathan is a former Deputy Governor.

s: Which body constituted the committee to curb unethical marketing in the pharma sector in October 2026?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: It was set up by the Department of Pharmaceuticals (Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers) and is headed by NITI Aayog Member M. Srinivas.

s: Which code guides ethical marketing practices in the pharmaceutical sector?
x: The Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices, 2024 guides ethical marketing; DPCO-2013 governs prices.

s: The Hockey India League, launched in 2013, was revived in which year after a seven-year break?
x: HIL began in 2013 and was revived in 2024 after a seven-year break.

s: Who chairs the RBI's Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets, announced on 4 November 2026?
o: RBI Deputy Governor in charge of Financial Markets Regulation
x: The committee is chaired by the RBI Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department.

s: Which markets does the RBI's Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (November 2026) cover?
o: Money, government securities, forex and related derivatives markets
x: Its remit is the RBI-regulated money, G-sec, foreign exchange and related derivatives markets and their infrastructure.

s: When was the Reserve Bank of India established?
x: RBI was set up on 1 April 1935; its HQ is Mumbai.

s: What was the foodgrain production target for 2026–27 announced by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan?
x: The foodgrain production target for 2026–27 was fixed at 373.93 million tonnes. The figure of 376.56 million tonnes refers to the record production in 2025–26, while 177.72 million tonnes is the Rabi target.

s: What is the principal cereal of Kharif crops, which are sown with the southwest monsoon?
x: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and rice is their main cereal; wheat is the main Rabi cereal.

s: NCRB's Crime in India 2024 (May 2026) is the first full-year data under which law?
x: Crime in India 2024 is the first full-year data under the BNS, 2023.

s: By how much did cybercrime rise as per NCRB's Crime in India 2024?
x: Cybercrime rose about 17.9%, while total cognisable crime fell about 6%.

s: Which organisation conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)?
x: PLFS is by the NSO under MoSPI; NFHS is coordinated by IIPS Mumbai.

s: Which body alone coordinated NFHS-6 (2023-24) for the first time?
x: NFHS-6, by the Health Ministry, was the first round coordinated solely by IIPS Mumbai.

s: Which of the following pairs (survey – conducting agency) is correctly matched?
x: ASER is by Pratham, an NGO; PLFS is by NSO (MoSPI) and NFHS-6 by the Health Ministry through IIPS Mumbai.

s: What was the overall unemployment rate (15+, CWS) as per the PLFS bulletin for September 2026?
x: Unemployment was 5.0% (rural 4.2%, urban 6.9%); it was 5.2% in September 2025.

s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index (2026)?
x: Gujarat topped IFI 2026 with 56.6, followed by Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha.

s: In NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: AP ranked 8th (48.7) and was a Frontrunner, not a Top Performer.

s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026 for the second year?
x: Odisha topped the Fiscal Health Index 2026 again; Punjab came last.

s: The 2026-27 foodgrain target of 373.93 MT is lower than which 2025-26 record?
x: The 2026-27 target (373.93 MT) is slightly lower than the 2025-26 record of 376.56 MT.

s: Which body does NITI Aayog's October 2026 report on the care economy recommend setting up?
x: The report recommends a National Care Council, a National Care Qualification Framework and a National Caregiver Registry.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's overall rank in NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index 2026?
x: AP was 8th overall (score 48.7) and placed as a 'Frontrunner'; Gujarat topped.

s: Which organisation publishes the Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI) report?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: ADSI is the companion report of NCRB's Crime in India; the 2024 edition recorded 1,70,746 suicides.

s: NFHS-6 (2023-24) covered all States and Union Territories except which State?
x: NFHS-6 surveyed about 6.8 lakh households in all States/UTs except Manipur.

s: Which body released the Fiscal Health Index 2026?
x: The Fiscal Health Index is published by NITI Aayog; its second edition (March 2026) placed Odisha at the top.

s: How many pillars and indicators does NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026 use?
x: IFI 2026 uses 8 pillars and 84 indicators across 28 States and 8 UTs.

s: Which State was placed last in NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026?
x: Odisha topped and Punjab was last in FHI 2026.

s: In which year was the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) launched?
x: NPHCE was launched in 2010-11.

s: In which year was the agreement behind the Pennaiyar water dispute between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka made?
x: The Pennaiyar dispute is linked to an 1892 agreement; Tamil Nadu sought a tribunal in November 2019.

s: The Union Home Minister proposed linking which river system sequence in the context of Interlinking of Rivers?
x: The proposal was to link rivers from the Brahmaputra to the Godavari and Cauvery. The Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar option is a separate link opposed by Kerala, not the Union Home Minister’s proposal.

s: In which year was the National Water Development Agency set up?
x: NWDA was set up in 1982; the National Perspective Plan (30 links) dates to 1980.

s: Which State opposed the Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar river-linking project over possible harm to the Vembanad wetland?
x: Kerala opposed the Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar link, citing possible harm to the Vembanad wetland.

s: Which of the following pairs (project – detail) is correctly matched?
o: Krishna Water Supply – Water to Hyderabad
Indira Gandhi Canal – Periyar in Kerala to Vaigai in Tamil Nadu
x: The Krishna Water Supply project supplies water to Hyderabad. Mullaperiyar diverts Periyar to Vaigai, and the Indira Gandhi Canal takes Sutlej–Beas water to Rajasthan.

s: How many river links did the National Perspective Plan (1980) identify?
x: The NPP (1980) identified 30 links: 14 Himalayan and 16 Peninsular; NWDA came in 1982.

s: The idea of interlinking Indian rivers goes back to whom?
x: The idea goes back to Sir Arthur Cotton in the 19th century; NWDA was set up in 1982.

s: The Mullaperiyar project diverts water from which river to which?
x: Mullaperiyar takes Periyar (Kerala) water to the Vaigai (Tamil Nadu).

s: The first post-Independence international cargo voyage from Bogibeel Terminal travelled through which route to reach Pangaon Port in Dhaka?
o: PM Gati Shakti GIS platform and the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route
Dhubri–Sadiya route and the National Logistics Policy corridor
NW-2 on the Brahmaputra and the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route
Coastal waterways and the National Transport Master Plan route
x: The voyage followed NW-2 on the Brahmaputra and then the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route to Pangaon Port, Dhaka. NW-2 extends from Dhubri to Sadiya and is associated with IWAI, but the other options do not describe the voyage route.

s: National Waterway-2 (Dhubri–Sadiya) on the Brahmaputra is how long?
x: NW-2 runs 891 km from Dhubri to Sadiya and is managed by IWAI.

s: Who flagged off the first post-Independence international cargo voyage from Bogibeel on 5 October 2026?
x: Sarbananda Sonowal flagged it off from Bogibeel Terminal, Dibrugarh; it carried methanol from APCL Namrup.

s: Which agency manages National Waterway-2 (Dhubri-Sadiya)?
x: NW-2 on the Brahmaputra is managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about elderly welfare in India?
o: Under the 2007 Senior Citizens Act, a senior citizen is a person aged 65 years or above.
Section 23 of the 2007 Act allows certain property transfers to be declared void.
Article 41 of the Constitution is associated with elderly welfare.
The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.
x: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 defines a senior citizen as a person aged 60 years or above, not 65.

s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), launched in 2008, has how many national missions?
x: The NAPCC (2008) comprises eight national missions; SAPCCs operate at the State level.

s: Which State became the first to introduce a dedicated comprehensive elderly care bill?
x: Kerala became the first State with a dedicated comprehensive elderly care bill.

s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers which combination of forms of abuse in the context of Kerala Police’s ‘Speak Up’ task force?
o: Physical, financial and cyber abuse, but not sexual or verbal abuse
Only verbal, emotional and economic abuse
Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse
x: The PWDVA, 2005 covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse. The other options omit one or more of these forms or introduce a limitation not stated in the law’s identified scope.

s: What punishment does Kerala's proposed comprehensive elderly care law provide for violations?
x: The proposed law covers abuse, neglect and illegal property occupation, mandates registration of old-age homes and provides for jail and fines.

s: Which Gram Panchayat was described as India's first net-zero panchayat in the context of panchayat-level climate action?
o: Gram Sabha of a Scheduled Area
A Gram Panchayat in Uttar Pradesh
x: Bela Gram Panchayat in Maharashtra was described as India's first net-zero panchayat, with initiatives including more than 90,000 trees, solar panels and waste segregation. Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka were also associated with initiatives, but the named panchayat was Bela.

s: Which of the following is included among the subjects in the Eleventh Schedule relevant to Panchayat-level development?
x: Non-conventional energy is among the subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule. Foreign trade, national defence, and currency and coinage are not the subjects identified in the Eleventh Schedule fact.

s: Which legislation empowers the Gram Sabha to protect community resources in Scheduled Areas?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
x: The PESA Act, 1996 provides for the Gram Sabha's role in protecting community resources in Scheduled Areas. The other options concern national climate missions, birth and death registration, and lottery regulation respectively.

s: In the action plan for a drug-free India, what approach was emphasised regarding drug trafficking?
o: Targeting only State-level offenders through a three-tier NCORD
Targeting only small offenders through a two-tier NCORD
Targeting whole networks and supply chains, along with strengthening the four-tier NCORD
Targeting only international suppliers through a single-tier NCORD
x: The strategy emphasised targeting whole networks and supply chains rather than only small offenders, while strengthening the four-tier NCORD. The other options incorrectly narrow the target or change the NCORD structure.

s: At the high-level meeting in Panaji, Goa, what was the target year set in the action plan for a drug-free India?
x: The action plan aims to achieve a drug-free India by 2029. The year 2047 is associated with the broader Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, not the drug-free India target.

s: Which Article concerns devolution to Panchayats for economic development and social justice?
x: Article 243G concerns devolution for economic development and social justice; panchayat climate plans are integrated into the GPDP.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – 2020; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Narcotics Control Bureau – 2020; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking – Directive Principle
x: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan began in 2020 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The NCB dates to 1986 (MHA), Article 47 is a Directive Principle, and the international day is June 26.

s: In which year was the Narcotics Control Bureau set up?
x: The NCB was set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Home Affairs to enforce the NDPS Act, 1985.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Women set up?
x: NCW was set up in 1992.

s: In which year was the NDPS Act enacted?
x: The NDPS Act dates from 1985; the NCB was set up in 1986.

s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment added which Part to the Constitution?
x: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX on Panchayats.

s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs, except for medicinal purposes?
x: Article 47 (a Directive Principle) asks the State to prohibit intoxicants injurious to health, except for medicinal use.

s: Under which Sections of the Press Council Act, 1978 did the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting nominate 13 journalists to the 15th Press Council of India in October 2026?
x: On 17 October 2026 the MIB nominated 13 journalists (six editors and seven working journalists) under Sections 5 and 6 of the Press Council Act, 1978.

s: Under the Press Council Act of which year was the Press Council of India first set up in 1966?
x: The PCI was first set up in 1966 under the Press Council Act, 1965; it can only warn, admonish or censure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 15th Press Council of India?
o: It has a Chairperson and 28 members.
Its members include 5 MPs: 3 from Lok Sabha and 2 from Rajya Sabha.
Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is its Chairperson since 24 April 2026.
National Press Day is observed on 26 November.
x: National Press Day is observed on 16 November, not 26 November; the other statements are correct.

s: How many members does each Department-Related Standing Committee (DRSC) reconstituted for 2026-27 have?
x: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on Defence for 2026-27?
x: Radha Mohan Singh heads the Defence committee; Bhartruhari Mahtab heads Finance and Shashi Tharoor heads External Affairs.

s: Of the 24 DRSCs reconstituted in October 2026, how many work under the Lok Sabha Speaker?
x: 16 DRSCs work under the Lok Sabha Speaker and 8 under the Rajya Sabha Chairman.

s: Who has been appointed Chief Commissioner of the Telangana Senior Citizens Commission in October 2026?
x: Justice E. Tirumala Devi, a retired High Court judge, is the Chief Commissioner for three years.

s: What salary deduction do government employees neglecting their parents face under Telangana's new senior citizens framework?
x: A 15% salary deduction, credited to the parents, applies to government employees who neglect them.

s: Who set up the seven-member committee to revive the Hockey India League in October 2026?
